title: Pebble app is causing 60min+ missed readings (possibly)
body:
Moto G5 plus, stock 7.0 phone.
Xdrip+ latest nightly builds, or latest stable version (Nov I think it is)

I may need to do more testing; but I think the pebble app is causing me to lose signal for 60min+. A restart collector occasionally works; swapping collector type [ob1/old] sometimes helps too. But usually needs a phone reboot to restore the connection.
This drop out can happen in different locations (home, work, car, etc) So I don't believe it to be interference from something specific. It can be at anytime of day/night. But usually only happens once in a day - 2 days (not several times a day/24hr period).

I first tried turning off the pebble watch, still had app installed. still had missed readings.
Removed the Pebble app; as recommended by @jamorham  and tested for about 36-48 hours & no large missed readings happened (several 10-15; but never more than about 15min)
After re-installing the pebble app I got a missed reading w/in a few hours, and again the next night.

I have been using this Moto for about a year. I used to get ~88% capture rate pre ob1; and ~98% post.

I have sent logs from xdrip in; I'm not sure if/how I can attach them here.

comments.body:
I don't think its the pebble app exactly. I expect it will be bluetooth resource starvation within Android.

Basically you can imagine that whenever android is hunting to connect to a bluetooth device it is using up a slot. Anything you have paired or any apps which are searching for peripheral devices will be using this up. Too many slots used up and bluetooth has problems.

Does your pebble app have watches in there you are not using? Do you have anything else paired in android bluetooth settings that you're not using? Try removing those if so.

Thanks.
I did just now delete all but a few watch faces. I use xdrip clay 98% of the time. When I take a dex break for a few days I use another face.
Let's see if that helps.

as for BT devices, I have a few paired with my phone. I use headphones 1-4times a week, so I want to keep them paired. as well as the onetouch meter. I could possibly remove the OBDii device until I need to use it on a car.

if it is BT congestion; are there xdrip setting(s) I can try?
